configuration.limitation: RA 11199 ss.4(a)(9), 8(i), 9(a) and 18; SSS Circular 2024-006 (business employers) and Circular 2024-007 (household employers), effective January 2025. Regular SS uses the first PHP20,000 monthly salary credit at 5% employee and 10% employer; excess to PHP35,000 belongs to SSS_MPF. Initial compulsory coverage extends through the 60th birthday. The first contribution liability date includes earlier employers and is independent of current registration. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/employees/ . Separation and retirement payments outside remuneration for services are excluded. A missing date of birth is charged as under sixty with a payslip warning (owner ruling). Circular 2024-007 gives household compensation below PHP5,000 nine distinct MSC brackets from PHP1,000 to PHP5,000; the household employer pays the full 15% regular SS share, while the employee pays zero. From PHP5,000 compensation, the regular employer/employee split applies. RA 10361 s.30 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514): a domestic worker is covered by SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG after at least one month of service — `months_through(service_start, last employed day of the period)` under 1.0 charges nothing. MSC is the monthly salary credit between PHP 4,000 and PHP 35,000; 5%/10% is the 2025 regular-employer split (Circular 2024-006). RA 11199 s.9(a): compulsory coverage begins for an employee not over sixty; a member covered before sixty keeps contributing while employed — the SSS standing election `covered_before_60` (recorded default false: unrecorded, no contribution past sixty). RA 10361 s.30 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514): a domestic worker is covered after at least one month of service — `person.household_first_month` (DOMESTIC terms, under one completed month at the start of the period) charges nothing.

warn_when.message: date of birth missing: SSS treats the employee as under 60.

SSS coverage past sixty cannot be determined: the employee was hired at sixty or later with no SSS charge on this payroll — record the election covered_before_60 if the member was covered before sixty (RA 11199 s.9(a)); nothing is charged until then.
SSS stops at sixty-five: the member has reached the compulsory retirement age (RA 11199 s.12-B(a)(2)); no SSS, MPF or EC is charged.

authority: RA 11199 ss.4(a)(9), 8(i), 9(a) and 18; SSS Circular 2024-006 (business employers) and Circular 2024-007 (household employers), effective January 2025. Regular SS uses the first PHP20,000 monthly salary credit at 5% employee and 10% employer; excess to PHP35,000 belongs to SSS_MPF. Initial compulsory coverage extends through the 60th birthday. The first contribution liability date includes earlier employers and is independent of current registration. Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/employees/ . Separation and retirement payments outside remuneration for services are excluded. A missing date of birth is charged as under sixty with a payslip warning (owner ruling). Circular 2024-007 gives household compensation below PHP5,000 nine distinct MSC brackets from PHP1,000 to PHP5,000; the household employer pays the full 15% regular SS share, while the employee pays zero. From PHP5,000 compensation, the regular employer/employee split applies. RA 10361 s.30 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514): a domestic worker is covered by SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG after at least one month of service — `months_through(service_start, last employed day of the period)` under 1.0 charges nothing. SSS Circular 2024-007 (https://www.sss.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Cir-2024-007-HR-Kasambahay-scaled.jpg): household compensation below ₱5,000 takes a salary credit of ₱1,000 below ₱1,250 and ₱500 brackets to ₱5,000 (`max(round(compensation, 500, HALF_UP), 1,000)`), the household employer paying the whole 15% and the kasambahay nothing (`person.household_low`); the SSS household-employer page deducts the employee share only "if earning more than P5,000.00". Owner ruling (opsph, 2026-10-07): a missing date of birth is treated as under sixty — SSS, MPF and EC are charged; RA 11199 s.9(a) covers every employee not over sixty, and an unrecorded birth date gives no ground to treat the person as over it. The payslip carries the warning (`warn_when`: date of birth missing). A foreign employee is covered like any other unless an SSS bilateral social security agreement exempts the person (SSS standing election `exempt_by_totalisation`, customer input; https://www.sss.gov.ph/employees/). Coverage past sixty (RA 11199 https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/86333, read 2026-10-07): s.9(a) makes coverage compulsory for employees "not over sixty (60) years of age" — the age at entry; s.11 ends the employer’s contribution only at separation; s.12-B(a) retires a member who has reached sixty and is separated, or who has reached sixty-five. So an employee covered before sixty keeps contributing while employed until sixty-five. `covered_before_60` is derived: hired before the sixtieth birthday (`employment.start_date`), or an SSS charge on this payroll in the twelve months before, or the election `covered_before_60` (an override, e.g. a member first covered through an earlier employer). From sixty-five nothing is charged. A warning names an employee of sixty or more for whom none of these holds.

The base is the BASIC line, which Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keeps whole against undertime, tardiness, leave without pay and absences (the ABSENCE and NO_PAY_LEAVE lines are not subtracted). PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶3 keys the premium off the basic monthly salary stated in the contract, whole for a mid-month hire or leaver (`person.terms.basic_salary`). name: Pag-IBIG Fund (Home Development Mutual Fund)

configuration.limitation: Republic Act 9679 ss.6–7 and HDMF Circular 460 (15 January 2024; contributions effective February 2024), pp.1–3: monthly Fund Salary is basic salary and other allowances received in the month. Employee contribution is 1% up to PHP1,500 and 2% above PHP1,500; employer contribution is 2%, with a PHP10,000 compensation ceiling. Republic Act 10361 s.30: domestic workers are covered after at least one month of service; where monthly Fund Salary is below PHP5,000, the employer pays both shares. Contributions use remuneration actually paid for the employment month, including covered allowances and deducting unpaid absence. Sources: https://wcms.dmw.gov.ph/uploads/DMW_ADVISORY_37_2025_01225b9fec.pdf ; https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/19155 ; https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514 Coverage history: HDMF Circular 460 C.1–2 (official DMW annex pp.2–4); Circular 274 B and H.2–4 (certified ONAR copy https://naro.law.upd.edu.ph/issuances/5476, p.8). Private initial coverage not over 60 is distinct from continuing membership until compulsory Fund retirement at 65. Non-compulsory termination permits mandatory re-enrolment when coverage resumes; self-paying and voluntary classes have no automatic employer payroll counterpart. Membership facts require a recorded evidence reference; missing registration never establishes exemption. RA 10361 s.30: where a domestic worker’s monthly Fund Salary is below ₱5,000 the employer pays both shares (`person.household_low`). RA 10361 s.30 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514): a domestic worker is covered after at least one month of service — `person.household_first_month` (DOMESTIC terms, under one completed month at the start of the period) charges nothing.

Age: the IRR of RA 9679 (https://web.archive.org/web/2023id_/https://www.pagibigfund.gov.ph/document/pdf/governance/43.1_on_institutional_matters/IRR%20of%20RA%20No.%209679.pdf, read 2026-10-07) Rule V s.1(a) makes membership mandatory for "all employees who are compulsorily covered by the SSS" (a private employee "not over 60 years old"), and s.10: "Any member shall be compulsorily retired under the Fund upon reaching age sixty-five (65)" — so nothing is charged from sixty-five, nor from sixty for an employee not covered before it (the SSS derivation). Voluntary membership after that (s.3) is the member’s, not payroll.

A WEEKLY or DAILY entity withholds each week or day on the Annex E weekly or daily column; the month-to-date liability is the part number × the column on the month-to-date base ÷ the part number, so equal weeks or days withhold exactly the column and unequal ones the column on their average (a recorded default: the engine charges the month to date). December’s last part annualises even when its week ends in January.

configuration.limitation: Charges nothing and is remitted to no one: its base records the contract’s minimum wage, month to date by calendar days (so every slip of a month, at any frequency or switch, carries a positive share), when the slip’s holder is a minimum wage earner on the period’s last day (the WTAX `person.mwe` test, restated), so the 1604-C alphalist can sort Schedule 2. A zero line is not listed on the payslip.

authority: NIRC s.24(A)(2); RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(B)(13) as amended by RR 11-2018 (https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/RR%20No.%2011-2018.pdf): a minimum wage earner is exempt on the statutory minimum wage and its holiday, overtime, night-shift and hazard pay, and the employer lists the MWEs separately in the 1604-C alphalist (Schedule 2, https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/1604C%20Alphalist%20Format%20-%20final.pdf).
